Start with the expanded examples. Open further examples for options and alternative R approaches.

char

Create characters from ASCII codes

Stata 

generate z = char(code)

R base 

data$z <- vapply(data$code,intToUtf8,character(1))

Differs from Stata Restricted to ASCII codes 1–127; extended-byte encodings are not Unicode code points.

Stata reference · R reference

clock

Text to a date-time

Stata 

generate t = clock(s, "YMDhms")

R lubridate 

mutate(data, t = lubridate::ymd_hms(s))

Differs from Stata R uses Date/POSIXct or tsibble calendar classes, not Stata numeric date/time counts from 1960; convert epochs and time zones when exchanging underlying numeric values.

Stata reference · R reference

Parse a date-time with an explicit UTC timezone

Stata 

generate double z = clock(s, "YMDhms")

R base 

data$z <- as.POSIXct(data$s,format='%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S',tz='UTC')

Differs from Stata POSIXct is seconds since 1970 with a timezone; Stata clock is milliseconds since 1960 without a timezone.

Stata reference · R reference

cofd

Convert R dates to Stata midnight millisecond codes

Stata 

generate double z = cofd(d)

R base 

data$z <- as.numeric(data$d-as.Date('1960-01-01'))*86400000

Differs from Stata Returns ordinary Stata %tc milliseconds since 1960, not a POSIXct object.

Stata reference · R reference

Text to a date

Stata 

generate d = date(s, "YMD")

R lubridate 

mutate(data, d = lubridate::ymd(s))

Differs from Stata R uses Date/POSIXct or tsibble calendar classes, not Stata numeric date/time counts from 1960; convert epochs and time zones when exchanging underlying numeric values.

Stata reference · R reference

Parse day-month-year date strings

Stata 

generate z = date(s, "DMY")

R base 

data$z <- as.Date(data$s,format='%d/%m/%Y')

Differs from Stata R Date objects use a different numeric origin from Stata; use the object for calendar operations, not raw-code comparison.

dofc

Convert Stata millisecond datetimes to dates

Stata 

generate z = dofc(milliseconds)

R base 

data$z <- as.Date(as.POSIXct(data$milliseconds/1000,origin='1960-01-01',tz='UTC'),tz='UTC')

Differs from Stata For ordinary Stata %tc values without leap-second encoding; UTC supplies a deterministic timezone.

Stata reference · R reference

dofm

First day of a monthly period

Stata 

generate d = dofm(m)

R tsibble 

mutate(data, d = as.Date(m))

Differs from Stata Here m is a tsibble::yearmonth() value. R uses Date/POSIXct or tsibble calendar classes, not Stata numeric date/time counts from 1960; convert epochs and time zones when exchanging underlying numeric values.

Stata reference · R reference

Convert Stata monthly codes to month-start dates

Stata 

generate z = dofm(m)

R base 

data$z <- as.Date(sprintf('%04d-%02d-01',1960L+data$m%/%12L,data$m%%12L+1L))

Differs from Stata R Date objects use a different numeric origin from Stata; use the object for calendar operations, not raw-code comparison.

Differs from Stata R Date objects use a different numeric origin from Stata; use the object for calendar operations, not raw-code comparison.

Day of the week

Stata

R lubridate

wday() counts Sunday as 1; Stata's dow() counts Sunday as 0.

format

Display a date

Stata 

format d %td

R base 

format(data$d, "%d%b%Y")

Dates keep their class; format() only changes how they print.

generate

Age or duration in years

Stata 

generate age = (d2 - d1) / 365.25

R lubridate 

mutate(data, age = lubridate::time_length(lubridate::interval(d1, d2), "years"))

Differs from Stata time_length(interval(...), "years") uses calendar-year lengths; dividing days by 365.25 is a fixed-length approximation and can give different ages.

Extract half-year numbers

Stata 

generate z = halfyear(d)

R base 

data$z <- (as.integer(format(data$d,'%m'))-1L)%/%6L+1L

Differs from Stata Accepts an R Date column and returns the demonstrated calendar component; raw Stata date codes require conversion first.

hh

Extract the hour from a UTC timestamp

Stata 

generate z = hh(t)

R base 

data$z <- as.integer(format(data$t,'%H',tz='UTC'))

Differs from Stata Input is an R POSIXct timestamp; convert raw Stata %tc numbers before extracting components.

lower

Lower case

Stata 

generate s = lower(name)

R stringr 

mutate(data, s = str_to_lower(name))

Differs from Stata R Unicode, regular-expression and case rules can differ from non-ustr Stata string functions; Stata empty strings are missing whereas R distinguishes empty strings and NA.

mofd

Monthly period from a date

Stata 

generate m = mofd(d)

R tsibble 

mutate(data, m = tsibble::yearmonth(d))

Differs from Stata tsibble::yearquarter() is the quarterly version, like qofd(). R uses Date/POSIXct or tsibble calendar classes, not Stata numeric date/time counts from 1960; convert epochs and time zones when exchanging underlying numeric values.

Convert Date values to Stata monthly codes

Stata 

generate z = mofd(d)

R base 

data$z <- (as.integer(format(data$d,'%Y'))-1960L)*12L+as.integer(format(data$d,'%m'))-1L

Differs from Stata Returns numeric months since January 1960, explicitly using Stata monthly units.

real

Text to a number

Stata 

generate x = real(s)

R base 

mutate(data, x = as.numeric(s))

Differs from Stata destring() from tidystata also strips value labels. as.numeric() warns for invalid text, unlike Stata real(); factors must be converted through their text levels before numeric conversion.

Stata reference · R reference

Parse a controlled decimal grammar with missing for invalid text

Stata 

generate z = real(s)

R base 

valid <- grepl('^[+-]?[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?$',data$s); data$z <- rep(NA_real_,length(valid)); data$z[valid] <- as.numeric(data$s[valid])

Differs from Stata Deliberately limited grammar avoids accidental warnings; scientific notation and tagged missing require extension.

Stata reference · R reference

regexm

Match a regular expression

Stata 

generate has = regexm(name, "^A")

R stringr 

mutate(data, has = str_detect(name, "^A"))

Differs from Stata R Unicode, regular-expression and case rules can differ from non-ustr Stata string functions; Stata empty strings are missing whereas R distinguishes empty strings and NA.

Stata reference · R reference

Flag strings containing only ASCII digits

Stata 

generate z = regexm(s, "^[0-9]+$")

R base 

data$z <- as.integer(grepl('^[0-9]+$',data$s))

Differs from Stata This simple shared regex is portable; Stata and R regex engines differ for advanced patterns.

Stata reference · R reference

regexr

Replace the first regular-expression match

Stata 

generate s = regexr(name, "[0-9]+", "")

R stringr 

mutate(data, s = str_replace(name, "[0-9]+", ""))

Differs from Stata str_replace_all() replaces every match, like ustrregexra(). R Unicode, regular-expression and case rules can differ from non-ustr Stata string functions; Stata empty strings are missing whereas R distinguishes empty strings and NA.

Stata reference · R reference

Replace the first numeric run in text

Stata 

generate z = regexr(s, "[0-9]+", "#")

R base 

data$z <- sub('[0-9]+','#',data$s)

Differs from Stata First-match regex replacement; advanced regex features differ across engines.

Stata reference · R reference

regexreplaceall

Replace all numeric runs in text

Stata 

generate z = regexreplaceall(s, "[0-9]+", "#")

R base 

data$z <- gsub('[0-9]+','#',data$s)

Differs from Stata StataNow regexreplaceall workflow with a simple ASCII pattern; older Stata versions use other functions.

Stata reference · R reference

regexs

Extract the matching text

Stata 

generate d = regexs(1) if regexm(name, "([0-9]+)")

R stringr 

mutate(data, d = str_extract(name, "[0-9]+"))

Differs from Stata str_extract() returns NA for nonmatches; Stata generate ... if leaves empty strings in those rows. regexs() also depends on the preceding regexm() match.

Stata reference · R reference

Extract the first capturing group

Stata 

generate z = regexs(1) if regexm(s, "([A-Z]+)-([0-9]+)")

R stringr 

data$z <- stringr::str_match(data$s,'([A-Z]+)-([0-9]+)')[,2]

R returns the group directly without a prior global regex-match state; unmatched rows use NA.

Stata reference · R reference

split

Split text into several variables

Stata 

split name, parse(" ")

R tidyr 

separate_wider_delim(data, name, delim = " ", names_sep = "_", too_few = "align_start")

Stata reference · R reference

Split two numeric fields and convert their types

Stata 

split s, parse("-") destring

R tidyr 

data <- tidyr::separate_wider_delim(data,s,delim='-',names=c('s1','s2'),cols_remove=FALSE); data$s1 <- as.integer(data$s1); data$s2 <- as.integer(data$s2)

Differs from Stata Requires exactly two clean integer fields; resulting column names s1 and s2 are fixed.

Stata reference · R reference

Split two-component delimited strings

Stata 

split s, parse("-") generate(part)

R tidyr 

data <- tidyr::separate_wider_delim(data, s, "-", names = c("part1", "part2"), cols_remove = FALSE)

Differs from Stata Name each part explicitly; too few or too many pieces are an error by default.

Stata reference · R reference

1 more examples and alternatives

Split two-component delimited strings

Stata 

split s, parse("-") generate(part)

R base 

parts <- strsplit(data$s,'-',fixed=TRUE); data$part1 <- vapply(parts,`[`,character(1),1); data$part2 <- vapply(parts,`[`,character(1),2)

Differs from Stata Fixed two-field example with exactly one delimiter per row; generated stub part is fixed.
